And in this year,
al-Hakim, the Caliph of Egypt, killed Barjawan the eunuch.
For this man, because of his excessive strictness towards al-Hakim,
would not allow him to ride out at improper times,
nor to give gifts to men without justification.
And on this account he became vexed with him,
and killed him.
Now the people of Egypt grieved greatly at his murder,
and they rioted and came to the gate of al-Hakim's palace.
And he, being afraid,
went up to the upper chamber,
and stood by one of the doors, and called out peace upon the people, and said:
"Treachery was made known to me concerning Barjawan,
and on this account I killed him.
And I beg of you
that you will be helpers to me, and not adversaries,
because I am still a youth."
And he wept before them,
and persuaded them,
and they desisted and went away.
And in order to gladden their hearts,
he brought Fahd, the Christian secretary,
and clothed him in royal robes,
and said to him
that he should not be troubled,
but just as he had been,
so should he administer the affairs of the kingdom.
Then after three years,
two Arab lawyers,
who were Abu Tahir and Ibn 'Addas,
accused Fahd to al-Hakim,
and he rebuked them.
They, however, incited others,
and they too brought accusations against the Christians.
And when he could no longer endure them,
he commanded, and Fahd was put to death.
And because this Fahd was very faithful and beloved to al-Hakim,
and he had been compelled by the urgency of the Arabs to kill him,
he sent, brought his sons, and clothed them [with robes of honour].
And he commanded that no one should molest them,
or approach their dwellings.
Then Ibn 'Addas gained power in Egypt,
and Abu Tahir in Syria.
And they inflicted many evils,
not only on the Christians,
but also on the Arabs,
especially with excessive and heavy weights,
so that they might raise the large sum that they had promised.
Now the Caliph's sister had a certain Egyptian secretary in Syria,
and he sent a complaint to her against Abu Tahir.
And she, because her brother listened to her greatly,
went in and began [to speak] to him.
And she obtained an order and sent and had Abu Tahir killed,
and his head was brought to Egypt,
and children dragged his corpse through the streets.
